question_text: In projectile motion, what is true about the velocity vector just before landing compared to just after launch, assuming level ground?

options.text:
(4)
It has the same magnitude but opposite vertical direction

explanation:

              launch but with the vertical component reversed in direction (downward instead of upward) due to symmetry,
              while the horizontal component remains unchanged.

question_text: In projectile motion, what is the direction of the velocity vector at the highest point of its trajectory?

options.text:
(3)
At an angle to the horizontal

explanation:
In projectile motion, the velocity has both horizontal (vx) and vertical (vy) components.
              At the highest point, the vertical component vy=0 due to the symmetry of the parabolic path,
              while the horizontal component vx remains constant. Thus, the velocity vector is purely horizontal.

options.text:
(4)

              revolutions per unit time. They are reciprocals, as f=1T or T=1f,
              defining their inverse relationship.

question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is responsible for keeping the object in its circular path?

              This force, directed towards the center, provides the necessary centripetal acceleration to change the
              direction of the velocity continuously.

question_text: For an object moving in a plane with constant acceleration, what is true about its velocity vector?

options.text:
(4)
It changes in magnitude and/or direction

explanation:
In motion with constant acceleration in a plane, the velocity vector changes in magnitude and/or
              direction over time because the acceleration continuously alters it. Unlike uniform motion, the velocity
              is not constant unless the acceleration is zero.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Motion in a Plane / Test 7

question_text: In projectile motion, what is the condition for achieving maximum horizontal range on level ground?
explanation:
The horizontal range R=v02sin⁡2θ0g is maximized when sin⁡2θ0=1,
              which occurs at 2θ0=90∘ or θ0=45∘. This angle balances the
              horizontal and vertical components for the greatest distance.
subject: Physics

question_text: What is the primary reason a projectile follows a curved path?
explanation:
The curved (parabolic) path of a projectile results from the constant acceleration due to gravity acting
              vertically, while the horizontal motion remains uniform. This combination of uniform horizontal motion and
              accelerated vertical motion produces the curve.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Motion in a Plane / Test 9

question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is the relationship between centripetal force and the object’s mass?

options.text:
(3)
It is proportional to mass squared

explanation:
The centripetal force is given by Fc=mv2R=mac, where m is the mass. Thus,
              the centripetal force is directly proportional to the mass of the object, meaning a greater mass requires
              a larger force to maintain the same motion.
subject: Physics

question_text: What is the nature of the acceleration in uniform circular motion?

options.text:
(4)
Constant in magnitude but not direction

explanation:
In uniform circular motion, the acceleration is centripetal, meaning it is directed towards the center of
              the circle. It changes direction continuously to remain radial but maintains a constant magnitude, as the
              speed is constant.

question_text: In projectile motion, at what point is the speed of the projectile minimum?
explanation:
The speed of a projectile is minimum at its maximum height because the vertical component of velocity (vy) is zero, leaving only the horizontal component (vx), which is constant. At all other
              points, the speed includes both components.

question_text: In motion with constant acceleration in a plane, what determines the path of the object?
explanation:
The path of an object in motion with constant acceleration in a plane depends on its initial velocity and
              the direction and magnitude of the constant acceleration. For example, zero initial velocity with constant
              acceleration results in a straight line, while non-zero initial velocity can produce a parabolic path
              (e.g., projectile motion).
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Motion in a Plane / Test 10

question_text: For an object in projectile motion, which component of acceleration is zero?
explanation:
In projectile motion, neglecting air resistance, the only acceleration is due to gravity, acting
              vertically downward. The horizontal component of acceleration is zero because there is no force acting
              horizontally to change the horizontal velocity.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Motion in a Plane / Test 10

question_text: In projectile motion, what is the angle between the velocity and acceleration vectors at the highest point?
explanation:
At the highest point, the velocity is purely horizontal (vy=0), while the acceleration (gravity)
              is vertical downward. Thus, the angle between them is 90°, as they are perpendicular.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Motion in a Plane / Test 10
